name: close-window-tabless
description: Cmd+Shift+W on a window whose space has no live tab must close it. Same fixture and palette-dismiss gate as quit-empty-no-palette.json - the auto-opened command palette would otherwise route the chord through its own kPassToMainMenu path and never test the browser window's own IDC_CLOSE_WINDOW handling at all.

actions.note: long enough that the auto-opened palette is definitely up before the dismiss attempts
ssh-launched Atrium is not always frontmost - without this the dismiss keys can land elsewhere
second dismiss attempt: scrim click clear of the panel and the sidebar
third dismiss attempt - repeat in case the first landed before the palette had key focus
quit-two-windows.json's own history is that the dismiss needs more like 4-6s to land on this VM
THE MEASUREMENT: IDC_CLOSE_WINDOW on a tabless space

assertions.label: palette-dismissed
assertions.note: GATE: without this the chord routes through the palette's kPassToMainMenu path, same trap quit-empty-no-palette.json exists to avoid

assertions.label: chord-reached-the-window
assertions.note: separates 'the window is still standing' from 'the chord never arrived at all' - the ambiguity that let a check pass against a scenario which had never run its own assertions

assertions.label: user-initiated-close-taken
assertions.pattern: Atrium: user-initiated close beats the last-tab-out keep-open
assertions.note: THE MEASUREMENT, positive half: OnWindowCloseRequested took the user-initiated branch rather than falling into the empty-strip suppression

assertions.label: suppression-did-not-fire
assertions.note: THE MEASUREMENT, negative half: the keep-open veto (Last-tab-out interception) must NOT have fired for this close - it still must for an automatic empty-strip close, just not this user-initiated one

assertions.label: browser-keep-alive-released
assertions.note: THE WINDOW IS REALLY GONE. This replaces an ax_window_count of 0, which could never answer here: axresize prints nothing for a windowless app AND nothing for a dead one, so the runner reports it as a harness error rather than a pass. The registry losing BROWSER is the evidence for this control. vlog_after, not vlog: the identical line appears at launch, before the browser registers its own keep-alive.

assertions.desc: LIVENESS: the app survived the close and still answers Cmd+Q. With no window left it is running on APP_CONTROLLER's keep-alive alone, which is what Chrome on macOS does after its last window closes.
